blocks.text: Plane 07 · Cron Substrate — what actually runs, what it schedules, and where it lies about doing so.

blocks.body: Cron jobs are session-only and silently expire after 7 days, but three subsystems assume they are durable. That mismatch is the root cause behind two of the four critical findings below.

blocks.text: Show me the evidence. Let's verify that.
This report traces the cron substrate from the scheduler entrypoint down to the jobs it silently drops, and states what a fix requires at each layer.

cards.body: In-memory job table, keyed per session.

blocks.title: How the false-pass actually happens
blocks.mermaid:
graph TD
  A[CronCreate fires] --> B[Job satisfies loop-gate]
  B --> C{7 days pass}
  C -->|job expires silently| D[Gate re-checks]
  D --> E[Non-empty CronList from a DIFFERENT job reads as healthy]
  E --> F[False pass]
  style F fill:#ef444433,stroke:#ef4444
blocks.caption: The gate cannot distinguish 'never armed' from 'armed and expired' — this is the mechanism, not just the symptom.

blocks.headline: loop-gate false-pass on expired job
blocks.evidence: MEASURED. `CronList()` returning non-empty is necessary but not sufficient — the check lives in `PostToolUse:CronList` and never distinguishes `never armed` from `armed and expired`, so a session-only job satisfies the gate for up to 7 days, then falsely re-passes on the NEXT check.

blocks.headline: no expiry notification — silent job death
blocks.evidence: MEASURED. `recurring:true` jobs fire once at expiry then are deleted from the in-memory table — no call to `hk__ping` or any other notification path, confirmed by tracing `CronCreate`'s own doc comment against observed behavior.

blocks.text: Open questions handed to the strategist: should the gate persist a durability token outside the session table? Is the 7-day cap a hard platform limit, or a deliberate session-lifetime bound worth documenting more loudly at CronCreate call time?
